definition: Accelerate runs the same PyTorch training script on one GPU, many GPUs, TPUs or with mixed precision, with only a few line changes.
details: Created by Sylvain Gugger at Hugging Face in 2021.

explainer.lead: How to install Accelerate, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import torch
from accelerate import Accelerator

accelerator = Accelerator(mixed_precision="bf16")
model = torch.nn.Linear(4, 1)
opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters())
data = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(torch.randn(64, 4), torch.randn(64, 1)), batch_size=8)
model, opt, data = accelerator.prepare(model, opt, data)

for x, y in data:
    loss = torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(model(x), y)
    accelerator.backward(loss)
    opt.step(); opt.zero_grad()

explainer.inAi: Also loads huge models across GPU, CPU and disk (device_map="auto"), which is how Transformers fits big LLMs on small machines.
explainer.jsNote: Accelerate is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.
